$comment: D-CSUBSET-FN-TYPE-TYPEDEF-PAREN-NAME (TF-C64): a parenthesized-NAME function-TYPE typedef `typedef int (BinOp)(int, int);` — the pervasive real-tcl.h shape (`typedef int (Tcl_AppInitProc)(Tcl_Interp*)`, ~90 instances). BinOp aliases the FUNCTION type (no `*`); the program uses it as tcl.h does — as the pointee of a callback parameter (`BinOp *op`) — and calls through it: apply(add,40,5)=45 then apply(sub,45,3)=42. ROOT CAUSE this witnessed: the (since retired, D-PP-FC2-ORACLE-RETIRE) compilation-unit type-name oracle seeded BinOp for a REPARSE of the tree that defines it, flipping `(BinOp)` from a parenthesized declarator (BinOp the NAME) to an abstract function-suffix param (BinOp a param TYPE) → S_DeclarationDeclaresNothing. Now a C file parses once and a declarator's name is bound when its declarator ends (C 6.2.1p7, D-C-A-DECLARATORS-NAME-IS-BOUND-AT-THE-END-OF-ITS-DECLARATION), so `(BinOp)` is read while BinOp is not yet a type name: the paren-name declarator. RED-ON-DISABLE: bind a declarator's name before its declarator ends → `(BinOp)` reads as an abstract parameter list → S_DeclarationDeclaresNothing → the program no longer compiles (compile failure, not exit 42); pinned at the unit tier by UnitTypeNames.AParenNameTypedefDeclaresItsName. The `release` arm re-witnesses the fn-type-typedef-typed indirect call survives the full shipped optimizer pipeline (inlining over the new FnSig-typedef shape).
